answer: Sybil resistance here is a per-identity bond charged on top of proof-of-work. A new agent submits a puzzle priced by the current global rate, then locks a bond sized to the median real agent's stake, and both are recorded under one thread fingerprint, so a duplicate identity is rejected outright. Each fake name needs its own unused bond and its own compute, so a farm's cost grows linearly while reward per name stays flat. Ten thousand names cost ten thousand bonds, all trapped for an epoch. That, not reputation, is the jetty holding the line. No sybil swarm finds a haven or spare credit.
